slots.label: The ability owner
slots.meaning: The Pokemon that owns the ability.

slots.label: The other Pokemon
slots.meaning: The attacker, target, opponent or source, as the trigger defines it.

slots.label: The move
slots.meaning: The move currently being used or resolved.

slots.label: The move user
slots.meaning: The Pokemon whose type, category and flags are read for the move.

slots.label: The damage
slots.meaning: The effective damage. For after-taking-damage this includes the multi-hit rewrite.

slots.label: The hit result
slots.meaning: How the hit turned out (normal, super effective, and so on).

slots.label: The stage change
slots.meaning: How many stages the stat moved.

slots.label: Simulation flag
slots.meaning: Whether the call is only a preview, with no side effects.

slots.label: The hit counters
slots.meaning: The hit count and hit index of a multi-hit move.

slots.label: The type matchup so far
slots.meaning: The type-chart multiplier the game has worked out so far for the move against the target (2 = super effective).

whens.label: When I enter the battle
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon comes into the battle, at the start or after a switch. Example: Intimidate lowers the foes' Attack as soon as it enters.

whens.label: When an ally enters the battle or is revived
whens.summary: Runs when my partner comes onto the field or is revived. Example: Commander hops into an ally Dondozo's mouth the moment Dondozo arrives.

whens.label: When a foe enters the field
whens.summary: Runs when an opposing Pokemon comes onto the field. Example: answer every new foe with a free move.

whens.label: When a wild Pokemon is created for an encounter
whens.summary: Runs while a wild Pokemon is being made for an encounter, before any battle starts. Example: Synchronize gives the wild Pokemon my nature.

whens.label: When my ability is lost or switched off
whens.summary: Runs when this ability is taken away, replaced or switched off while the Pokemon stays on the field. Example: Illusion ends when Gastro Acid hits.

whens.label: When I am about to enter the battle
whens.summary: Runs just before this Pokemon appears, while the game still prepares the entry. Example: prepare a disguise before the Pokemon shows up.

whens.label: When a battle begins
whens.summary: Runs once when a new battle begins, before the first turn. Example: reset a form at the start of every battle.

whens.label: When the battle ends
whens.summary: Runs once when the battle is over. Example: Pickup-style abilities hand out loot after the win.

whens.label: When I switch out
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon is recalled to the party. Example: Regenerator heals a third of max HP when it switches out.

whens.label: When I leave the field
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon leaves the field in any way: switching out, fainting or being forced out. Example: end a weather it created.

whens.label: When I faint
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon faints, with the attacker when a move did it. Example: Aftermath hurts the attacker for a quarter of its max HP.

whens.label: When every turn ends
whens.summary: Runs at the end of every turn this Pokemon is on the field. Example: Speed Boost raises Speed by 1 stage each turn.

whens.label: When a turn starts, before anyone moves
whens.summary: Runs at the start of a turn, before anyone moves. Example: choose a free move before the foes act.

whens.label: When I wake up
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon wakes from sleep. Example: raise Attack the first time it wakes up.

whens.label: When I flinch
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon flinches and loses its move. Example: Steadfast raises Speed by 1 stage after a flinch.

whens.label: When the berries of the turn have been eaten
whens.summary: Runs after the berries of the turn have been eaten. Example: Cud Chew eats last turn's berry again at this moment.

whens.label: When I eat a berry
whens.summary: Runs after this Pokemon eats a berry. Example: Cheek Pouch heals a third of max HP right after a berry.

whens.label: When I am about to use a move
whens.summary: Runs just before this Pokemon uses a move, once the move is chosen. Example: change my type to match the move I am about to use.

whens.label: When my chosen move starts
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon's chosen move starts to execute. Example: lock the Pokemon into its first move, like Gorilla Tactics.

whens.label: When my attack lands
whens.summary: Runs after this Pokemon's attack lands on a target. Example: Poison Touch may poison the target after a contact hit.

whens.label: When I knock out a Pokemon
whens.summary: Runs after this Pokemon knocks out a Pokemon, or any Pokemon faints. Example: Moxie raises Attack by 1 stage after a knockout.

whens.label: When I win the fight
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon's side wins the fight. Example: earn bonus prize money after winning.

whens.label: When anyone uses a move
whens.summary: Runs after any Pokemon on the field uses a move. Example: Dancer copies a dance move that was just used.

whens.label: When I inflict a status condition
whens.summary: Runs after this Pokemon gives a foe a status condition. Example: confuse a foe right after it gets burned.

whens.label: When I am hit
whens.summary: Runs after a move has hit this Pokemon. Example: Static may paralyze an attacker that made contact.

whens.label: When I take any damage
whens.summary: Runs after this Pokemon takes any damage, from a move or not. Example: Wimp Out switches me out when a hit drops my HP below half.

whens.label: When I take a critical hit
whens.summary: Runs when a critical hit lands on this Pokemon. Example: Anger Point raises Attack to the maximum after a critical hit.

whens.label: When a hit is about to land on me
whens.summary: Runs just before a hit lands on this Pokemon, when the game still lets the ability react. Example: change my type to resist the incoming move.

whens.label: When I get a status condition
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon gets a status condition. Example: Synchronize passes the burn back to whoever caused it.

whens.label: When I lose my held item
whens.summary: Runs when this Pokemon loses its held item. Example: use a free move when my item is knocked off.

whens.label: When Intimidate hits me
whens.summary: Runs when a foe's Intimidate lands on this Pokemon. Example: Competitive raises Sp. Atk by 2 stages after an Intimidate.

whens.label: When the weather changes
whens.summary: Runs when the weather changes. Example: Forecast changes Castform's form to match the new weather.

whens.label: While a weather is on, every turn
whens.summary: Runs every turn while a weather is active. Example: Rain Dish heals 1/16 of max HP each turn in the rain.

whens.label: When the terrain changes
whens.summary: Runs when the terrain changes. Example: Quark Drive gets a boost when Electric Terrain is set.

whens.label: When the biome changes
whens.summary: Runs when the run moves to a new biome. Example: set the weather again after every biome change.

whens.label: When one of my stats changes
whens.summary: Runs when one of this Pokemon's stats goes up or down. Example: Defiant raises Attack by 2 stages when a foe lowers a stat.

whens.label: When my ally's stat changes
whens.summary: Runs when one of my partner's stats goes up or down. Example: raise my own Attack when someone lowers my ally's stats.

whens.label: When a foe raises a stat
whens.summary: Runs when a foe raises one of its stats. Example: Opportunist copies the boost for myself.

whens.label: When a foe switches out
whens.summary: Runs when an opposing Pokemon is about to switch out. Example: strike a foe with a move as it leaves.

whens.label: While the game picks who a move targets
whens.summary: Runs while the game picks who a move targets. Example: Lightning Rod draws every Electric move to me.

whens.label: While the game calculates my move's priority
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out a move's priority. Example: Gale Wings gives Flying moves +1 priority at full HP.

whens.label: While the game decides if I jump the turn order
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides whether this Pokemon jumps the turn order. Example: Quick Claw sometimes lets me move first.

whens.label: While the game checks if a foe can escape
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a foe may switch or run. Example: Arena Trap stops every foe from leaving.

whens.label: While the game rolls my chance to run away
whens.summary: Runs while the game rolls this Pokemon's chance to flee a wild battle. Example: Run Away always succeeds.

whens.label: While the game rolls the chance of a double battle
whens.summary: Runs while the game rolls whether a wild encounter is a double battle. Example: Arena Trap makes doubles four times as likely.

whens.label: While the game calculates my weight
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out this Pokemon's weight. Example: Heavy Metal doubles it, which changes Heavy Slam.

whens.label: While the game calculates burn damage on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the damage burn does to this Pokemon at turn end. Example: Heatproof halves it.

whens.label: While the game checks if burn weakens my attacks
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether burn halves my attacks. Example: Guts keeps full strength while burned.

whens.label: While the game calculates how long my status lasts
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how long a status lasts. Example: Early Bird makes sleep end twice as fast.

whens.label: While the game calculates a berry's healing
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how much a berry heals. Example: Ripen doubles the healing of berries I eat.

whens.label: While the game checks if my berry should be eaten
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks at what HP a pinch berry is eaten. Example: Gluttony eats it at half HP instead of a quarter.

whens.label: While the game calculates a move's power
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out a move's power, before damage. Example: Technician raises the power of 60-power moves by 1.5.

whens.label: While the game calculates damage I deal
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the damage this Pokemon deals. Example: multiply the damage of every hit by 1.3.

whens.label: While the game calculates damage I take
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the damage this Pokemon takes. Example: Multiscale halves the damage at full HP.

whens.label: While the game calculates same-type attack bonus
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the same-type attack bonus. Example: Adaptability makes the bonus 2x instead of 1.5x.

whens.label: While the game calculates critical hit stage
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the critical hit level of a move. Example: Super Luck adds 1 level.

whens.label: While the game calculates critical hit damage
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how much extra damage a critical hit does. Example: Sniper makes crits hit 1.5 times harder.

whens.label: While the game decides if a hit is critical
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides whether a hit is critical. Example: always land a critical hit against a poisoned foe, like Merciless.

whens.label: While the game decides how many times a move hits
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides how many times a move hits. Example: Parental Bond adds a second, weaker strike.

whens.label: While the game rolls how many hits a multi-hit move gets
whens.summary: Runs while the game rolls the hits of a 2 to 5 hit move. Example: Skill Link always gives the maximum 5 hits.

whens.label: While the game calculates my move's accuracy
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how accurate this Pokemon's move is. Example: Compound Eyes multiplies accuracy by 1.3.

whens.label: While the game calculates accuracy against me
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how accurate a move aimed at this Pokemon is. Example: Wonder Skin makes status moves 50% accurate.

whens.label: While the game calculates my move's effect chance
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the chance of this Pokemon's move extra effect. Example: Serene Grace doubles it.

whens.label: While the game calculates effect chance against me
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the chance of an extra effect against this Pokemon. Example: Shield Dust sets it to 0.

whens.label: While the game rolls the random damage spread
whens.summary: Runs while the game rolls the random damage spread of a hit. Example: foes always roll the lowest damage against me.

whens.label: While the game applies weather damage changes to my move
whens.summary: Runs while the game applies weather damage changes to a move. Example: a Fire move keeps full power in the rain.

whens.label: While the game calculates one of my stats
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out one of this Pokemon's stats. Example: Huge Power doubles Attack.

whens.label: While the game calculates a foe's stat
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out a stat of a foe. Example: an aura that lowers every foe's Speed by 10%.

whens.label: While the game calculates a stat of a Pokemon on my side
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out a stat of any Pokemon on my side. Example: Plus and Minus-style auras boost my whole team.

whens.label: While the game calculates the recoil I take
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out the recoil this Pokemon takes. Example: Reckless-style abilities scale recoil up or down.

whens.label: While the game applies the foe's stat stages
whens.summary: Runs while the game applies a foe's stat changes to the damage. Example: Unaware ignores the foe's boosts.

whens.label: While the game picks the stat my attack uses
whens.summary: Runs while the game picks the stat my attack uses. Example: Body Press-style abilities attack with Defense.

whens.label: While the game decides if my move is physical or special
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides whether a move is physical or special. Example: use the higher of Attack and Sp. Atk to pick.

whens.label: While the game rates my attack against the target's types
whens.summary: Runs while the game rates how well my attack matches the target's types. Example: bone moves hit immune types for full damage.

whens.label: While the game checks whether my move can miss
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a move is allowed to miss. Example: No Guard makes every move hit.

whens.label: While the game picks my defensive stat
whens.summary: Runs while the game picks the stat this Pokemon defends with. Example: defend with Speed instead of Defense.

whens.label: While the game picks the foe's defensive stat
whens.summary: Runs while the game picks which defense of the foe my attack hits. Example: hit the weaker of the foe's Defense and Sp. Def.

whens.label: While the game calculates how far my stats move
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how many stages a stat change moves. Example: Simple doubles every change, Contrary flips it.

whens.label: While the game decides a move's type
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides a move's type. Example: Pixilate turns Normal moves into Fairy moves.

whens.label: While the game calculates type matchup against me
whens.summary: Runs while the game works out how well an incoming move matches this Pokemon's types. Example: Tera Shell caps every hit at not very effective.

whens.label: While the game checks whether a move can hit me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a move can hit this Pokemon at all. Example: Levitate blocks Ground moves.

whens.label: While the game checks the foe's type immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks the foe's immunity to my move's type. Example: Scrappy lets Normal moves hit Ghost types.

whens.label: While the game applies my own type chart to my attacks
whens.summary: Runs while the game applies my own type chart to my attacks. Example: my attacks count as super effective against one type.

whens.label: While the game decides whether my move ignores abilities
whens.summary: Runs while the game decides whether my move ignores the target's ability. Example: Mold Breaker ignores Levitate.

whens.label: While the game checks if a stat drop can land on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a stat drop can land on me. Example: Clear Body blocks every drop a foe causes.

whens.label: While the game checks if my stat is protected
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether one of my stats is protected from a drop. Example: Keen Eye protects accuracy.

whens.label: While the game checks if my side's stat is protected
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a stat of my side is protected. Example: Flower Veil protects Grass-type partners.

whens.label: While the game checks if a stat drop is reflected
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a stat drop is bounced back. Example: Mirror Armor sends the drop to the attacker.

whens.label: While the game checks if Intimidate lands on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether Intimidate lands on me. Example: Inner Focus blocks the Attack drop.

whens.label: While the game checks if a status can land on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a status can land on me. Example: Insomnia blocks sleep.

whens.label: While the game checks my status immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks my immunity to chosen statuses. Example: Limber blocks paralysis.

whens.label: While the game checks my side's status immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether my side is immune to a status. Example: Sweet Veil keeps my partner awake.

whens.label: While the game checks type-based status immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks type-based status immunity. Example: Corrosion poisons Steel and Poison types.

whens.label: While the game checks if a battle effect can land on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a battle effect such as confusion can land on me. Example: Own Tempo blocks confusion.

whens.label: While the game checks my battle-effect immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks my immunity to chosen battle effects. Example: Oblivious blocks infatuation and taunt.

whens.label: While the game checks my side's battle-effect immunity
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether my side is immune to a battle effect. Example: Aroma Veil protects my partner from Taunt.

whens.label: While the game checks if weather damage hurts me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether weather damage hurts me. Example: Sand Veil takes no damage in a sandstorm.

whens.label: While the game checks if weather affects me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a weather affects me at all. Example: be unaffected by the weather's side effects.

whens.label: While the game checks if weather is suppressed
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether the weather is switched off. Example: Cloud Nine cancels every weather effect.

whens.label: While the game checks if an interaction is blocked
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a move interaction is blocked. Example: block an interaction a move would normally have.

whens.label: While the game checks if I can be critically hit
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether I can be critically hit. Example: Battle Armor blocks critical hits.

whens.label: While the game checks if my item can be stolen
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether my held item can be taken. Example: Sticky Hold keeps the item.

whens.label: While the game checks if indirect damage hurts me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether indirect damage hurts me. Example: Magic Guard blocks poison, weather and recoil damage.

whens.label: While the game checks if a one-hit KO works on me
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a one-hit KO move works on me. Example: Sturdy makes Fissure fail.

whens.label: While the game checks if I can be forced out
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether I can be forced out. Example: Suction Cups ignores Roar and Whirlwind.

whens.label: While the game checks if explosive moves are blocked
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether explosive moves are blocked. Example: Damp stops Explosion and Self-Destruct.

whens.label: While the game checks if a berry can be eaten
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a berry may be eaten. Example: Unnerve stops the foes from eating berries.

whens.label: While the game checks if a status move is bounced back
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether a status move is bounced back. Example: Magic Bounce reflects Toxic.

whens.label: While the game checks if my move bypasses screens
whens.summary: Runs while the game checks whether my move passes screens and Substitute. Example: Infiltrator ignores Reflect.

whens.label: While the game prepares a hit against me
whens.summary: Runs while the game prepares a hit against this Pokemon, before type and damage are worked out. Example: block a move that meets a rule.

whens.label: While the game prepares my attack
whens.summary: Runs while the game prepares this Pokemon's attack, before type and damage are worked out. Example: change a stat used for the hit.

whens.label: While the ability is active
whens.summary: Always on while this ability is active; the game just looks for it. Example: Levitate keeps the Pokemon off the ground.

conditions.label: {who} is at full HP
examples: Halve damage at full HP
conditions.summary: Yes when the chosen Pokemon has all of its HP. A single missing HP counts as not full. Example: Multiscale halves damage only at full HP.

conditions.label: {who} has at most {pct}% HP

params.label: How the HP line is rounded

optionLabels.floor-half: Rounded down to a whole HP

formula.expr: exact: hp * 100 <= maxHp * pct ; floor-half: hp <= floor(maxHp * pct / 100) ; rounded-ratio: getHpRatio() <= pct / 100, getHpRatio() = Math.round(hp / maxHp * 100) / 100
formula.source: src/field/pokemon.ts:2408 (getMaxHp), :2430 (getHpRatio for rounded-ratio); integer math, no float ratio except rounded-ratio

examples: Boost power when at most 33% HP
conditions.summary: Yes when HP is at or below the percent you set, counted in whole HP. Example: at most 33% of 100 max HP is 33 HP or less.

conditions.label: {who} has at least {pct}% HP

params.label: How the HP line is rounded

optionLabels.floor-half: Rounded down to a whole HP

formula.expr: exact: hp * 100 >= maxHp * pct ; floor-half: hp >= floor(maxHp * pct / 100) ; rounded-ratio: getHpRatio() >= pct / 100, getHpRatio() = Math.round(hp / maxHp * 100) / 100
formula.source: src/field/pokemon.ts:2408 (getMaxHp), :2430 (getHpRatio for rounded-ratio); integer math, no float ratio except rounded-ratio

examples: Resist hits while above 75% HP
conditions.summary: Yes when HP is at or above the percent you set, counted in whole HP. Example: at least 50% of 101 max HP needs 51 HP.

conditions.label: {who} has between {minPct}% and {maxPct}% HP

params.label: How the HP line is rounded

optionLabels.floor-half: Rounded down to a whole HP

formula.expr: at-least(minPct) && at-most(maxPct), same rounding for both

examples: Heal only while between 10% and 50% HP
conditions.summary: Yes when HP is inside a range of percents, ends included. Example: between 10% and 50% of 200 max HP is 20 to 100 HP.

conditions.label: {who} just dropped below {ratio} of max HP

params.label: HP line (0.5 = half of max HP)
How the HP line is rounded

optionLabels.floor-half: Rounded down to a whole HP

formula.expr: exact: hp + damage >= maxHp * ratio && hp - calculateShellBellRecovery(pokemon) < maxHp * ratio ; floor-half: t = floor(maxHp * ratio); hp <= t && hp + damage > t ; damage-value: t = toDmgValue(maxHp * ratio) = max(floor(maxHp * ratio), 1); hp <= t && hp + damage > t
formula.source: src/data/abilities/ab-attrs.ts hpCrossedBelow (moved from PostDamageForceSwitchAbAttr.canApply); floor-half form from archetypes/berserk-on-threshold.ts. The Shell Bell term belongs to the exact form.

examples: Switch out when HP drops below 35%
conditions.summary: Yes when the hit that just landed pushed HP from above the line to at or below it. Example: HP 60 to 40 of 100 max crosses the 50% line.

conditions.label: The move is {type} type

params.label: Use the type after ability changes

examples: Boost Fire-type moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move is of the chosen type. Example: Water Absorb checks for a Water move.

conditions.label: The move is {category}
examples: Resist special moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move is physical, special or a status move. Example: Assault Vest-style effects only care about special moves.

conditions.label: The move has the {flag} property

formula.expr: move.doesFlagEffectApply({ flag: MoveFlags[flag], user: moveUser, target })
formula.source: src/data/moves/move.ts:986 (doesFlagEffectApply, so contact-ignoring abilities and substitutes count)

examples: Trigger only on contact moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move has a property, such as making contact, biting or sound, counting any property an ability adds. Example: Tough Claws boosts contact moves.

conditions.label: The move's power is {cmp} {n}
examples: Boost moves with 60 power or less
conditions.summary: Yes when the move's power passes the comparison. Example: power at most 60 is true for Quick Attack (40).

conditions.label: The move deals damage
examples: Only react to damaging moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move deals damage, which means it is physical or special. Example: a status move like Growl is a no.

conditions.label: The move targets {kind}

formula.expr: single: OTHER|NEAR_OTHER|RANDOM_NEAR_ENEMY ; all-foes: ALL_NEAR_ENEMIES|ENEMY_SIDE ; all-others: ALL_NEAR_OTHERS|ALL_OTHERS ; user-or-ally: USER|NEAR_ALLY|USER_AND_ALLIES ; field: BOTH_SIDES|USER_SIDE

examples: Only single-target moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move aims at a broad group such as one foe, all foes, everyone else or the field. Example: spread moves aim at all foes.

conditions.label: The move is aimed at {target}

params.label: How the move is aimed
options: the foe's side of the field
the user or an adjacent ally
the Pokemon that last hit the user

formula.expr: move.moveTarget === MoveTarget[target]  (one exact aim; use several of these in an ANY group for a set such as Ole's single-target test: one adjacent Pokemon, one other Pokemon, one adjacent foe, the foe's side)

examples: Only when the move is aimed at one adjacent foe
conditions.summary: Yes when the move is aimed exactly as chosen, such as one adjacent foe or all foes. Example: Earthquake aims at all other Pokemon.

conditions.label: The move's priority is {cmp} {n}
examples: Block priority moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move's printed priority passes the comparison. Example: priority above 0 is true for Quick Attack (+1).

conditions.label: The move hits more than once
examples: Only for multi-hit moves
conditions.summary: Yes when the move hits more than once this turn. Example: Bullet Seed with 3 hits.

conditions.label: This is hit number {cmp} {n}
examples: Only on the first hit
conditions.summary: Yes when the number of the current hit passes the comparison. Example: hit number 2 or higher means every strike after the first.

conditions.label: This is the final hit of the move
examples: Trigger after the final hit of a multi-hit move
conditions.summary: Yes on the final hit of a move. Example: the third strike of a 3-hit move.

conditions.label: The move's effectiveness is {cmp} {n}x
examples: Take less damage from super effective moves (Filter)
conditions.summary: Yes when the move's type matchup against the target passes the comparison. Example: at least 2 means super effective, like Filter checks.

conditions.label: The move has the {flag} property as printed

formula.expr: move.hasFlag(MoveFlags[flag])  (NOT doesFlagEffectApply: Long Reach style abilities and substitutes do not change it)

examples: A burn only on moves that never make contact, even when the attacker has Long Reach
conditions.summary: Yes when the move itself has the property as printed, whatever abilities add. Example: Bulletproof only looks at the move's own ball-and-bomb flag.

conditions.label: The move heals its user by a share of the damage it deals
examples: Plant Leech Seed after a draining move like Drain Punch
conditions.summary: Yes when the move heals its user by part of the damage, like a draining move. Example: Drain Punch and Giga Drain.

conditions.label: The hit dealt damage to the target

formula.expr: hitResult is EFFECTIVE, SUPER_EFFECTIVE, NOT_VERY_EFFECTIVE or ONE_HIT_KO (not a status move, a miss or an immune target)

examples: Only react when the hit really damaged me, not when a status move like Growl reaches me
conditions.summary: Yes when the hit connected and hurt: normal, super effective, not very effective or a one-hit KO. Missed, blocked and status hits are a no.

conditions.label: {who} took a critical hit

formula.expr: !!pokemon.turnData?.attacksReceived?.[0]?.critical  (the first hit that Pokemon took this turn; the default reads the other Pokemon)
formula.source: src/data/elite-redux/archetypes/chance-status-on-hit.ts ChanceStatusOnAttackAbAttr.canApply (critRequired); damage-reduction-generic.ts crit kind (Bad Omen reads the defender)

examples: Burn the target only when my attack was a critical hit
conditions.summary: Yes when the chosen Pokemon took a critical hit this turn. Example: burn the target only when my attack was a critical hit.

conditions.label: The move has a secondary effect chance
examples: Boost moves that have an extra effect
conditions.summary: Yes when the move has an extra effect that happens by chance. Example: Flamethrower can burn, so it is a yes.

conditions.label: The move is {moveId}
examples: Only when the move is Earthquake

guards.label: Not when my own move paid the HP
guards.why: Self-inflicted HP costs are not damage taken from a foe; triggering would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing when the HP was spent by my own move. Example: Belly Drum does not trigger Wimp Out.

guards.label: Not when the attacker's move already forces a switch
guards.why: The move switches the Pokemon out itself before the ability would act.

formula.expr: other has a last move AND it is not [DRAGON_TAIL, CIRCLE_THROW] AND not (SKY_DROP with result OTHER)

guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing when the attacker's move already forces a switch. Example: Dragon Tail already moved me out.

guards.label: Not when Sheer Force removed the move's extra effects
guards.why: Sheer Force removes secondary effects, and this effect counts as one.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing when the attacker's move is boosted by Sheer Force. Example: a Sheer Force Flamethrower leaves the effect off.

guards.label: Only after the last hit of a multi-hit move
guards.why: Reacting to every strike of a multi-hit move would trigger early and repeatedly.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: waits for the last hit of a multi-hit move against me. Example: Bullet Seed with 5 hits triggers after hit 5.

guards.label: Not once I have fainted
guards.why: A fainted Pokemon cannot change form or act; triggering would be a bug, not a design choice.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing once this Pokemon has fainted. Example: a fainted Pokemon never changes form.

guards.label: Only for Castform (Forecast) and Cherrim (Flower Gift)
guards.why: The weather forms exist only on those two species; on any other Pokemon there is no form to change to.

formula.expr: (species === CASTFORM && ability === FORECAST) || (species === CHERRIM && ability === FLOWER_GIFT)

guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only Castform with Forecast and Cherrim with Flower Gift can change weather form.

guards.label: Not when the target ignores extra effects (Shield Dust)
guards.why: Adding an effect to a Pokemon the game promises is immune to extra effects would be a bug, not a design choice.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: skips a target that ignores extra effects, like Shield Dust. Example: no flinch on a Shield Dust Pokemon.

guards.label: Not when the target is the user itself
guards.why: An effect meant for an opponent must never land on the user; that would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing when the move's target is the user. Example: an effect meant for foes never lands on me.

guards.label: Only when a Pokemon caused the status
guards.why: There is nobody to pass the status back to; running the effect would be a bug.

formula.expr: Boolean(other)  (the source Pokemon of the status)

guards.summary: Locked safety rule: needs a Pokemon that caused the status. Example: a burn from weather has no one to pass it back to.

guards.label: Only when the hit connected
guards.why: A move that missed or was blocked did nothing to react to; reacting would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only reacts when the hit connected. Example: a missed or blocked move does nothing.

guards.label: Only when the hit connected on a different Pokemon
guards.why: A miss, a block or a hit on the user itself is not an attack on a foe; reacting would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only reacts when the hit connected on a different Pokemon. Example: a hit on myself does not count.

guards.label: Only when the hit took away more than 0 HP
guards.why: Reacting to a hit that did no damage (a block, a Substitute, a status move) would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only reacts when the hit took away more than 0 HP. Example: a hit on a Substitute is ignored.

guards.label: Only when a different, standing Pokemon was hurt
guards.why: Reacting to damage on the user itself or on a Pokemon that already fainted would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only reacts when the move hurt a different Pokemon that is still standing. Example: not on a fainted target.

guards.label: Only after the last hit of my own multi-hit move
guards.why: Reacting to every strike of my own multi-hit move would trigger early and repeatedly.

formula.expr: !(holder.turnData.hitsLeft > 1)  (the holder is the attacker for an after-my-attack trigger)

guards.summary: Locked safety rule: waits for the last hit of my own multi-hit move. Example: Triple Axel triggers after hit 3.

guards.label: Only when a Pokemon's move knocked me out
guards.why: The faint can also come from poison, weather or recoil, with no attacker to react to; triggering would be a bug.

formula.source: src/phases/faint-phase.ts:256 (dispatches without attacker and move after indirect damage); bernerd-roster-mechanics.ts MutualDestructionPostFaintAbAttr.guards

guards.summary: Locked safety rule: needs a Pokemon's move to have knocked me out. Example: poison or weather faints do not count.

guards.label: Not when the attacker has already fainted
guards.why: Retaliating against a Pokemon that is already out of the fight would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing when the attacker already fainted. Example: no retaliation against a fainted foe.

guards.label: Only when I knocked the fainted Pokemon out myself
guards.why: The game tells every Pokemon on the field when something faints; without this rule bystanders would heal and loot.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: only I get the reward for a knockout I caused. Example: bystanders do not heal when a foe faints.

guards.label: Not when I am protected from indirect damage
guards.why: Chip damage must never get through an ability that promises to block all of it; that would be a bug.
guards.summary: Locked safety rule: does nothing to a Pokemon protected from indirect damage. Example: Magic Guard ignores the chip damage.
